REM-TELNET-001.title: Disable Telnet management access
REM-TELNET-001.summary: Remove Telnet from every administrative access path and rely on SSH.

cisco_ios.note: Apply to every VTY range. A device with two VTY blocks can permit Telnet on one while the other is SSH-only.

juniper_junos.note: Confirm an SSH session is available before committing, or you may lose remote access.

fortinet_fortios.note: allowaccess replaces the whole list, so restate every protocol you intend to keep.

REM-TELNET-001.generic: Locate the setting that governs which protocols may reach the administrative interface, and remove Telnet from it. Verify an encrypted alternative such as SSH is working first.

REM-SNMP-002.title: Remove default SNMP community strings
REM-SNMP-002.summary: Delete the well-known 'public' and 'private' communities and move to SNMPv3.

commands: snmp-server user <user> SECURE v3 auth sha <auth-pass> priv aes 128 <priv-pass>
cisco_ios.note: Update every monitoring system that polls this device before removing the old communities.

commands: set snmp v3 usm local-engine user <user> authentication-sha authentication-password <auth-pass>
set snmp v3 usm local-engine user <user> privacy-aes128 privacy-password <priv-pass>
juniper_junos.note: Update your NMS to poll with SNMPv3 credentials before committing.

fortinet_fortios.note: List existing entries with 'show system snmp community' to find the id to delete.

REM-SNMP-002.generic: Delete any community string matching a vendor default and replace community-based polling with SNMPv3 using authentication and privacy.

REM-SSH-001.title: Restrict SSH to protocol version 2

cisco_ios.note: Requires an RSA key of at least 2048 bits; generate one with 'crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048' if none exists.

commands: set system services ssh protocol-version v2

fortinet_fortios.note: Availability of this setting varies by FortiOS release; confirm with 'show full-configuration system global'.

REM-SSH-001.generic: Configure the SSH server to accept only protocol version 2.

REM-HTTP-001.title: Disable the plaintext HTTP management server

cisco_ios.note: Enabling the secure server first avoids losing web management entirely.

commands: set system services web-management https system-generated-certificate
juniper_junos.note: Replace the system-generated certificate with a CA-issued one for production use.

fortinet_fortios.note: Removing http from allowaccess disables the plaintext administrative interface.

REM-HTTP-001.generic: Disable the unencrypted web administration listener and ensure the HTTPS equivalent is available first.

REM-SNMP-001.title: Disable SNMP v1 and v2c

commands: snmp-server user <user> SECURE v3 auth sha <auth-pass> priv aes 128 <priv-pass>
cisco_ios.note: Run 'show running-config | include snmp-server community' to enumerate every community first.

commands: set snmp v3 usm local-engine user <user> authentication-sha authentication-password <auth-pass>

fortinet_fortios.note: Configure an SNMPv3 user under 'config system snmp user' before removing v2c access.

REM-SNMP-001.generic: Remove community-string based SNMP access and configure SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy.

REM-AUTH-001.title: Protect privileged mode with a hashed secret
REM-AUTH-001.summary: Replace reversible privileged passwords with a strong hash.

cisco_ios.note: 'enable secret' supersedes 'enable password'; remove the latter so it cannot be used.

juniper_junos.note: Junos prompts for the password and stores only its hash. Do not use plain-text-password-value, which writes the credential into the configuration.

fortinet_fortios.note: FortiOS stores administrator credentials hashed; no reversible privileged password exists to remove.

REM-AUTH-001.generic: Ensure privilege escalation requires a credential stored as a strong one-way hash rather than a reversible encoding.

REM-AUTH-002.title: Encrypt stored passwords
REM-AUTH-002.summary: Prevent credentials being written to the configuration in cleartext.

cisco_ios.note: Type 7 encoding is reversible and only stops shoulder-surfing. Migrate local accounts to 'username <name> algorithm-type scrypt secret <pass>' for real protection.

commands: set system login user <user> authentication plain-text-password
juniper_junos.note: Entering the password interactively stores only its hash. Replace any existing plain-text-password-value entries.

REM-AUTH-002.generic: Ensure locally stored credentials are hashed rather than written into the configuration in readable form.

REM-AUTH-003.title: Enforce a minimum password length
REM-AUTH-003.summary: Require locally defined accounts to use passwords of at least 12 characters.

cisco_ios.note: Applies to passwords set after the command; existing credentials are unaffected and must be reset.

commands: set system login password change-type character-sets

REM-AUTH-003.generic: Configure the password policy to require at least 12 characters.

REM-AUTH-004.title: Configure centralised AAA
REM-AUTH-004.summary: Authenticate administrators against a central TACACS+ or RADIUS service.

commands: aaa authentication login default group CORP-GROUP local
aaa authorization exec default group CORP-GROUP local
cisco_ios.note: Keep the 'local' fallback so the device stays reachable if the AAA server is unavailable. Test in a second session before closing the first.

juniper_junos.note: Listing 'password' after 'tacplus' preserves local login if the server is unreachable.

fortinet_fortios.note: Add the RADIUS server to an administrator user group to take effect.

REM-AUTH-004.generic: Point administrative authentication at a central identity service, retaining a local fallback account.

REM-AUTH-005.title: Remove well-known default accounts
REM-AUTH-005.summary: Delete or rename predictable account names.

cisco_ios.note: Create and test the replacement account before deleting the old one, or you risk locking yourself out.

commands: set system login user <new-admin-name> class super-user
set system login user <new-admin-name> authentication plain-text-password
juniper_junos.note: Verify the new account can log in from a separate session before committing the deletion.

fortinet_fortios.note: FortiOS refuses to delete the account you are currently logged in as; log in as the replacement first.

REM-AUTH-005.generic: Create a uniquely named administrative account, verify it works, then remove the default-named one.

REM-LOG-001.title: Enable local logging
REM-LOG-001.summary: Retain log messages on the device.

commands: service timestamps log datetime msec localtime show-timezone
cisco_ios.note: Timestamps with the timezone make local logs correlatable with the central collector.

commands: set system syslog file messages any notice
set system syslog file messages authorization info

fortinet_fortios.note: Use 'config log disk setting' instead on models with local storage.

REM-LOG-001.generic: Enable local log retention with timestamps.

REM-LOG-002.title: Forward logs to a remote collector
REM-LOG-002.summary: Ship log messages off the device so they survive reboot and tampering.

cisco_ios.note: Pinning the source interface keeps the collector's ACLs stable.

commands: set system syslog host <syslog-ip> any info

fortinet_fortios.note: Reliable mode uses TCP, which avoids the silent loss possible with UDP syslog.

REM-LOG-002.generic: Configure at least one external syslog destination and confirm messages are arriving.

REM-LOG-003.title: Log administrative actions
REM-LOG-003.summary: Record configuration changes and privileged commands for attribution.

cisco_ios.note: 'hidekeys' keeps credentials out of the change log.

commands: set system syslog file interactive-commands interactive-commands any
set system syslog host <syslog-ip> interactive-commands any

fortinet_fortios.note: Administrative events appear in the FortiOS event log; confirm the event log is enabled and forwarded.

REM-LOG-003.generic: Enable configuration-change and command accounting, and forward those records to the central collector.

REM-NTP-001.title: Configure a time source
REM-NTP-001.summary: Synchronise the device clock so log timestamps are correlatable.

cisco_ios.note: Configure at least two sources so a single failure does not leave the clock drifting.

REM-NTP-001.generic: Configure at least two NTP servers and set the device timezone explicitly.

REM-NTP-002.title: Authenticate NTP associations
REM-NTP-002.summary: Prevent a spoofed time source from shifting the device clock.

cisco_ios.note: The key must match the one configured on the NTP server.

commands: set system ntp authentication-key 1 type md5 value <ntp-key>

REM-NTP-002.generic: Configure a shared authentication key with your NTP servers and mark it trusted.

REM-ACL-001.title: Restrict management access to trusted sources
REM-ACL-001.summary: Permit administrative sessions only from designated management networks.

cisco_ios.note: Confirm your own source address falls inside the permitted range before applying, or the session will drop.

commands: set firewall filter PROTECT-RE term mgmt from source-address <mgmt-network>
set firewall filter PROTECT-RE term mgmt from protocol tcp destination-port ssh
set firewall filter PROTECT-RE term mgmt then accept
set firewall filter PROTECT-RE term default then discard
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet filter input PROTECT-RE
juniper_junos.note: 'commit confirmed 5' rolls back automatically after five minutes unless confirmed, which protects you from locking yourself out.

fortinet_fortios.note: An administrator with no trusthost set is reachable from anywhere; set it on every account.

REM-ACL-001.generic: Restrict the management interface so it accepts connections only from the designated administration network.

REM-TIMEOUT-001.title: Set an idle session timeout

cisco_ios.note: 'exec-timeout 0 0' means the session never expires; apply the timeout to console and VTY lines alike.

REM-TIMEOUT-001.generic: Configure the administrative idle timeout to ten minutes or less.

REM-BANNER-001.title: Display a legal login banner
REM-BANNER-001.summary: Present an authorised-use notice before authentication.

commands: WARNING: Authorised access only. All activity is monitored and recorded.
Disconnect immediately if you are not an authorised user.
cisco_ios.note: Do not disclose the hostname, model or OS version in the banner; that information helps an attacker.

commands: set system login message "WARNING: Authorised access only. All activity is monitored and recorded."
set buffer "WARNING: Authorised access only. All activity is monitored and recorded."

REM-BANNER-001.generic: Configure a pre-authentication banner stating that access is restricted and monitored.

REM-SVC-001.title: Disable IP source routing

cisco_ios.note: IOS enables source routing by default, so this must be set explicitly.

REM-SVC-001.generic: Disable processing of source-routed IP packets.

REM-SVC-002.title: Disable legacy small servers
REM-SVC-002.summary: Turn off the echo, chargen and discard diagnostic services.

cisco_ios.note: Disabled by default since IOS 12.0, but worth stating explicitly in a hardened baseline.

REM-SVC-002.generic: Disable the legacy TCP and UDP small services if the platform provides them.

REM-SSH-002.title: Enable SSH for management

cisco_ios.note: A hostname and domain name must be set before an RSA key can be generated.

commands: set system services ssh protocol-version v2
set system services ssh root-login deny
juniper_junos.note: Denying direct root login forces administrators to authenticate as themselves first.

REM-SSH-002.generic: Enable the SSH service and ensure it is reachable on the management interface.

REM-SSH-003.title: Restrict SSH to strong ciphers
REM-SSH-003.summary: Remove weak ciphers and key exchange algorithms from the negotiable set.

commands: ip ssh server algorithm encryption aes256-gcm aes128-gcm aes256-ctr aes192-ctr aes128-ctr
ip ssh server algorithm mac hmac-sha2-256 hmac-sha2-512
ip ssh server algorithm kex diffie-hellman-group14-sha1 ecdh-sha2-nistp256
cisco_ios.note: Supported algorithm names vary by IOS release; check 'ip ssh server algorithm encryption ?' on the device.

commands: set system services ssh ciphers [ aes256-ctr aes192-ctr aes128-ctr ]
set system services ssh macs [ hmac-sha2-256 hmac-sha2-512 ]

fortinet_fortios.note: strong-crypto restricts both SSL and SSH to stronger algorithms.

REM-SSH-003.generic: Configure the SSH server to offer only AES-CTR or AES-GCM ciphers and SHA-2 MACs, removing 3DES and CBC modes.

REM-HTTPS-001.title: Enable HTTPS for web management
REM-HTTPS-001.summary: If a web interface is required, serve it over TLS only.

commands: set system services web-management https system-generated-certificate
juniper_junos.note: Replace the self-signed certificate with a CA-issued one before production use.

REM-HTTPS-001.generic: Enable the TLS web administration listener and disable its plaintext counterpart.
